title: Data entry scenario ab test basics
topic: Data entry scenario ab test basics
question: Walk through how you'd set up and evaluate this test, and what would make you confident the new button color actually caused any difference you see.
idealAnswer:
Randomly assign visitors to control, blue, or treatment, orange, so the two groups are comparable except for the button color

Decide the success metric upfront, e.g. click-through rate, and how it will be measured consistently for both groups

Determine a reasonable sample size or test duration in advance rather than stopping as soon as a difference appears, to avoid false positives from peeking early

Use a statistical test, e.g. a two-proportion test, to check whether the observed difference is unlikely to be due to random chance, considering both the p-value and effect size

Mentions confounding factors, e.g. running the test only on weekdays or only for one traffic source, that could bias results if not controlled for

Use a statistical test, e.g. a two-proportion test, to check whether the observed difference is unlikely to be due to random chance, considering both the p-value and effect size
Mentions confounding factors, e.g. running the test only on weekdays or only for one traffic source, that could bias results if not controlled for
followUps: The orange button wins with a p-value of 0.04 after you peeked at the results daily for two weeks. Why might that result be less trustworthy than it looks?
